questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I applied in the third round so at that time I could not take the chance of applying for a uni with only few spots. I applied for Prague because it had 75 spots, I like the city and I really just wanted to go on exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. Charles University had given me an appropriate amount of information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had received some emails with details about what to do and what not to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't that easy but not extremely difficult as well. I went for a private flat. A lot of scammers on facebook so it is great if one knows one who has been to Prague before.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great! I loved it but maybe there is not so much social life as opposed to living on campus but I dont quite know because I did not live there but I can imagine

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were given a time slot to come by on the first day to get our arrival documents signed. I could get my document signed before my quite late time slot so it wasn't a problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are people who can help you at uni both people working there and other exchange students. The administrative personel is not good at English so do not expect that much help from them,

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to apply for all new courses because the ones that I had found were not available.... But there is a lot of courses so I did not worry

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect not to get the courses you initially wanted but dont be stressed by it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses differ in levels. Some are relatively low work (no obligatory readings) but others are more demanding. The courses do not have as heavy a work load as in CPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much less student interaction which was sad.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Russian politics and society
War, the State and Society II
Geopolitics of Great Powers: Russia
Security Issues in Japan and the South East Asia
Strategic Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Geopolitics of Great Powers: Russia: Great teacher!! The most engaging and demanding that I had but loved it.
Security Issues in Japan and the South East Asia: The issues are really interesting and there is quite a low work load
Strategic Studies: The teacher was American and he was a true expert. It was very interesting and a lot of student activity.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Danish phone subscribtion abroad is a bit of a complex thing but I managed. Look into it before going. Data is not cheap in CZ.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was quite as expected acutally. Food was cheaper than back home but clothes and stuff like that are not.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use them but they did not expose us to any options

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus in Prague - there is a lot of social stuff like tours around CZ and parties

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You have to go travel CZ when you are here but also neighbouring countries!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Find friends and go drink beer new places each weekeend!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Difficult with the language but it wasn't a problem for me. Most speak good English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Seek them out yourselves! Classes wont let you socialise because there are no breaks in class were you can socialise and people are busy so they leave straight after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cheap beers and the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It is not all about the studies. Go traveling and explore the country and neighbouring countries.
2. Befriend people from your classes - they are great especially other exchange students
3. Do not stress about uni and the administrative part of it. It is fairly easy to take care of.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being away frome home so I could plan everything on my own (and my girlfriend) who was also here at the same time hehe. I really just love Prague. It is a beautiful city but not so big so you can actually manage to visit all parts of the city fairly easy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being to old to get student discounts.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
